incidents.summary: An April cyberattack stole M&S customers’ personal data, prompting collective legal action, while the company attributed the incident to human error.

sources.title: M&S cyber attack: Class action over data breach affecting millions | STV News
sources.quote: Thompsons Solicitors said it is launching a class action lawsuit against the retail giant after a catastrophic data breach in April that saw personal details belonging to millions of customers stolen by cyber criminals.

sources.title: M&S cyber attack: Class action over data breach affecting millions | STV News
sources.quote: M&S has since admitted that the incident was the result of “human error” and said the fallout is expected to cost the company around £300m.

sources.title: M&S cyber attack: Class action over data breach affecting millions | STV News
sources.quote: The stolen information included names, email addresses, postal addresses, and dates of birth.

incidents.summary: Labour groups accused M&S of continuing relationships with Thai suppliers linked to unresolved wage theft and failing to conduct adequate due diligence.

sources.title: Thailand: Over 900 garment workers denied $7.6 million severance as global brands face accountability calls - Business and Human Rights Centre
sources.quote: Next and Marks & Spencer were accused of continuing business relationships with factories linked to unresolved wage theft in Thailand, despite long-standing ties to Body Fashion Limited.

sources.title: Thailand: Over 900 garment workers denied $7.6 million severance as global brands face accountability calls - Business and Human Rights Centre
sources.quote: Labour groups allege the brands failed to conduct adequate due diligence while sourcing from Robert Ng–owned suppliers implicated in rights violations affecting over 900 workers.

incidents.summary: An M&S–Oxfam supply-chain study identified weak worker voice, inadequate social support, unfair promotion processes and working poverty among workers in India and the UK.

sources.title: Want to know how workers feel about working conditions? Ask them
sources.quote: UK-based retailer Marks & Spencer and non-profit Oxfam undertook a unique partnership to learn about human rights and worker well-being from workers in the company’s supply chain from food manufacturing sites in the UK and footwear factories in India.

sources.title: Want to know how workers feel about working conditions? Ask them
sources.quote: a lack of effective worker voice, fears about speaking out and raising concerns to managers, inadequate social supports like sick pay, a lack of transparency and fairness in promotion processes

sources.title: Want to know how workers feel about working conditions? Ask them
sources.quote: the prevalence of workers living in “working poverty,” i.e. not earning enough to adequately support themselves and their families.

positives: M&S partnered with Oxfam to study supply-chain workers’ experiences and publicly shared the findings.
M&S invested £1 million in a cattle-diet initiative intended to reduce methane emissions.
